subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should Telegram reaction prompt behavior remain derived from `reactionLevel` plus `reactionNotifications`, or should OpenClaw add an independent `reactionGuidance` configuration contract?
rationale: The existing controls already separately govern outbound reaction capability and incoming event visibility, while incoming events do not themselves start a turn; only maintainers can define whether another durable public setting and interaction promise are warranted.

options.title: Compose existing controls
options.body: Use `reactionLevel` for outbound guidance and condition a factual incoming-reaction note on enabled notifications, without adding a third user setting.

options.title: Add a prompt-only control
options.body: Add `reactionGuidance` only after specifying its precedence, defaults, upgrade behavior, and relationship to passive reaction events.

options.title: Defer to reaction-input design
options.body: Leave prompt semantics unchanged until the broader reaction-triggered-turn work establishes what reactions may cause an agent to do.

recommendation.title: Compose existing controls
recommendation.body: Use `reactionLevel` for outbound guidance and condition a factual incoming-reaction note on enabled notifications, without adding a third user setting.

likelyOwner.reason: The contribution guide assigns the Telegram area to this owner, and the decision spans Telegram behavior, configuration, and user-facing documentation.
